providers.title: The dyadic triangular Hilbert form on L^3 (OpenAI)
providers.scope: For every finite set S of scales and real F_0, F_1, F_2 in L^3(R_+^2), the sum over k in S and over admissible triples I of |L_I(F_0, F_1, F_2)| is at most 40 prod ||F_v||_3. Proved in the last lesson.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Local forms as traces
providers.scope: For step functions on atoms of level m and an admissible triple of scale k >= m + 1, L_I = 2^(2k) tr(D_0 W_0 D_1 W_1 D_2 W_2).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The four children of an admissible triple
providers.scope: The admissible children have sign triples with product 1; conditionally on one sign, each other sign is uniform; every admissible triple has exactly one admissible parent.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: One scale
providers.scope: For L^3 inputs, the sum over the admissible triples of one scale of |L_I| is at most prod ||F_v||_3.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Hessian of tr(P^(3/2))
providers.scope: d Phi_P(K) = (3/2) tr(sqrt P K) and d^2 Phi_P(K, K) = b_P(K) = (3/2) sum K_ij^2/(sqrt p_i + sqrt p_j); Phi is convex on positive semidefinite matrices.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Monotonicity of the inverse and the square root
providers.scope: For positive definite X <= Y, Y^{-1} <= X^{-1} and sqrt X <= sqrt Y.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Order comparison of Hessians (OpenAI)
providers.scope: If P <= aQ with a >= 1, every K supported on P is supported on Q and b_P(K) >= a^(-1/2) b_Q(K).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Midpoint gap
providers.scope: If -T <= U <= T, then (Phi(T + U) + Phi(T - U))/2 - Phi(T) >= b_T(U)/(2 sqrt 2).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Mixed trace estimate (OpenAI)
providers.scope: For maps W_v around a triangle and symmetric contractions D_v, |tr(D_0 W_0 D_1 W_1 D_2 W_2)| <= (5/3) sum_v b_{T_v}(U_v), with row stars R_v, T_v = R_v^T R_v and U_v = R_v^T D_v R_v; the constant does not depend on the dimensions.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Local energy increase (OpenAI)
providers.scope: The average energy of the four children exceeds the energy of an admissible triple by delta(I) >= 0, and |tau(I)| <= (10 sqrt 2/3) delta(I).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Total energy and telescoping
providers.scope: J_k = sum over admissible I of 2^(2k) e(I) is at most 2 sqrt 2 sum ||F_v||_3^3, and the weighted energy increases at scale k add up to J_(k-1) - J_k.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
